newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela inflation seen 2 pct a month by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inflation seen 2 pct a month by year-end.

text.p: Venezuelan Central Bank President Antonio Casas said on Friday that inflation would slow to about 2.0 percent a month by year-end, despite higher-than-expected data in October.
Casas said inflation would likely close 1996 at the upper end of the government's target of 1.5 to 2.0 percent per month.
"It may be reached, the two percent level," Casas told Reuters Financial Television after a conference here. "The important thing is the (lower inflation) tendency continues."
Venezuelan inflation rose 4.2 percent in October, up from a 3.6 percent increase in September. Venezuelan analysts had expected October inflation to run between 3.6 and 4.0 percent.
"It was above our original expectations, but we knew that we could have a hump," Casas said.
"The tendency for a lowering of prices is there and we can see it. Those sectors that are not affected directly by electricity increases are going down."
The central banker added that he saw a slight recovery in domestic demand to-date, but expected a larger rebound after the first quarter of next year.
"You have to have one major target when you have a stabilization program, which is a short-term program," he said. "The major target right now is lower inflation."
Casas said the central bank needed greater flexibility in its open market operations and called for a different kind of instrument that would acceptable to market.
